fixes.explanation: Revenge belongs to a different man, friend. The man in verse 4 killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him. The passage does turn to someone else in verse 11, a man who hates his neighbor, lies in wait, attacks him and kills him. Keep those two men apart in your head and the rest of the chapter gets a lot easier.

That's it, baker. Verse 12 says the elders of his city must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die. This is the man from verse 11 who hates his neighbor and lies in wait. So no city shelters him. The shelter in verses 4 to 6 was for the man who killed by accident.

Twelve is a big number, friend, and I'd love that many cookie trays, but the text says three. Israel is to set apart three cities within the land the LORD is giving them to possess. Verse 3 adds roads and three regions, so a man on the run can reach one of them. I think that's the point of the roads: nobody should be stuck wondering how to get there. A city is no help if you can't find the way in.
